subsection_title: Introduction
text:
FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS (FAQ)
The Most Common Questions Asked by International Professional Truck Drivers
This section answers the questions that international drivers ask us most often before
travelling to Germany.
If your question is not answered here, please contact EuroJobsCenter before making any
important decisions.

subsection_title: 1. Why does Germany need professional truck drivers?
text:
1. Why does Germany need professional truck drivers?
Germany has a high demand for qualiﬁed professional truck drivers. Many transport and
logistics companies are looking for experienced drivers.

subsection_title: 2. Is my job guaranteed?
text:
2. Is my job guaranteed?
No.
Employment depends on your professional qualiﬁcations, your performance and the
needs of your employer.
No recruitment agency or employer can legally guarantee permanent employment.

subsection_title: 3. Will my employer test my driving skills?
text:
3. Will my employer test my driving skills?
Yes.
Many employers carry out a practical driving assessment before assigning a company
vehicle.
This is a normal safety procedure.

subsection_title: 4. What happens if I fail the driving assessment?
text:
4. What happens if I fail the driving assessment?
Every employer has its own procedures.
Some employers may provide additional training, while others may decide not to
continue the employment relationship.

subsection_title: 5. Can I change employers later?
text:
5. Can I change employers later?
Yes, in many cases.
If the applicable legal requirements are fulﬁlled and the necessary procedures are
completed, changing employers is often possible.

subsection_title: 6. Do I have to leave Germany if my first job ends?
text:
6. Do I have to leave Germany if my ﬁrst job ends?
Not automatically.
Many professional drivers continue working for another employer after completing the
required legal procedures.

subsection_title: 7. Who decides whether I may change employers?
text:
7. Who decides whether I may change employers?
The competent German authorities make decisions regarding residence and
employment matters in accordance with German law.

subsection_title: 8. Is Code 95 impossible to obtain?
text:
8. Is Code 95 impossible to obtain?
No.
Every year, thousands of international drivers successfully obtain the required
qualiﬁcation.

subsection_title: 9. Can I obtain a Driver Card?
text:
9. Can I obtain a Driver Card?
Yes.
If you meet the applicable legal requirements, you can generally obtain a Driver Card.

subsection_title: 10. Will someone help me with Code 95?
text:
10. Will someone help me with Code 95?
Yes.
Your employer, EuroJobsCenter or an experienced training provider can explain the
available options.

subsection_title: 11. Will my employer help me after I arrive?
text:
11. Will my employer help me after I arrive?
Many employers provide support during the ﬁrst days, such as accommodation,
registration or company orientation.
The level of support depends on the employer.

subsection_title: 12. Will I receive accommodation?
text:
12. Will I receive accommodation?
Many employers assist international drivers in ﬁnding suitable accommodation.
The exact arrangements vary from company to company.

subsection_title: 13. Will I receive health insurance?
text:
13. Will I receive health insurance?
Yes.
Legally employed workers in Germany are generally covered by the German health
insurance system.

subsection_title: 14. Will I pay taxes?
text:
14. Will I pay taxes?
Yes.
Employees working legally in Germany pay taxes and social security contributions in
accordance with German law.

subsection_title: 15. Can my salary increase?
text:
15. Can my salary increase?
Yes.
Many employers increase salaries based on experience, performance and additional
qualiﬁcations.

subsection_title: 16. Can I receive bonuses?
text:
16. Can I receive bonuses?
Yes.
Some employers offer bonuses for safe driving, attendance, good performance or
special assignments.

subsection_title: 17. Can I obtain additional qualifications?
text:
17. Can I obtain additional qualiﬁcations?
Yes.
Many drivers later obtain ADR, tanker, heavy haulage or other professional
qualiﬁcations.

subsection_title: 18. Should I bring cash to Germany?
text:
18. Should I bring cash to Germany?
It is advisable to have enough money to cover your personal expenses during your ﬁrst
days.

subsection_title: 19. Should I keep copies of my documents?
text:
19. Should I keep copies of my documents?
Yes.
Always keep copies of your passport, visa, driving licence and important employment
documents.

subsection_title: 20. What should I do if I do not understand something?
text:
20. What should I do if I do not understand something?
Ask questions.
Never make assumptions about legal or employment matters.

subsection_title: 21. Can I contact EuroJobsCenter after arriving in Germany?
text:
21. Can I contact EuroJobsCenter after arriving in Germany?
Yes.
Whenever possible, EuroJobsCenter will continue to provide guidance and support
during your transition.

subsection_title: 22. Can someone pretend to represent EuroJobsCenter?
text:
22. Can someone pretend to represent EuroJobsCenter?
Unfortunately, yes.
Always verify the identity of anyone requesting money or personal documents.

subsection_title: 23. Should I pay money to private individuals?
text:
23. Should I pay money to private individuals?
No.
Always follow the official payment procedure explained in this handbook.

subsection_title: 24. Why is the recruitment fee deposited with an escrow trustee?
text:
24. Why is the recruitment fee deposited with an escrow trustee?
The escrow system provides additional ﬁnancial security for both the applicant and
EuroJobsCenter.

subsection_title: 25. What happens if my visa is refused?
text:
25. What happens if my visa is refused?
The escrow procedure will be handled in accordance with the agreed escrow
arrangement.

subsection_title: 26. What should I do if I become ill?
text:
26. What should I do if I become ill?
Inform your employer immediately and follow the company's reporting procedures.

subsection_title: 27. What is the most important quality of a professional driver?
text:
27. What is the most important quality of a professional driver?
Professionalism.
Reliable, honest and respectful drivers are highly valued.

subsection_title: 28. How can I build a successful career in Germany?
text:
28. How can I build a successful career in Germany?
Drive safely.
Respect the law.
Keep learning.
Communicate honestly.
Treat everyone with respect.

subsection_title: 29. What should I do if I have doubts?
text:
29. What should I do if I have doubts?
Stop.
Ask questions.
Verify the information before making any important decision.

subsection_title: 30. What is EuroJobsCenter's most important advice?
text:
30. What is EuroJobsCenter's most important advice?
Be patient.
Be honest.
Be professional.
Germany offers excellent opportunities for qualiﬁed truck drivers who are willing to work
hard, respect the law and continue learning throughout their careers.

subsection_title: Final Message
text:
FINAL MESSAGE
Starting a new life in another country is a big step.
You are not expected to know everything before you arrive.
This handbook has been prepared to answer your most important questions and help
you begin your new career with conﬁdence.
If you still have questions, please contact EuroJobsCenter before making important
decisions.
We wish you a safe journey and every success in Germany.
